title: challenge: cross-invocation respawn cap finding (T-0918 review)
spec: A reviewer of task/T-0918 claimed: run_worker in orchestrator/spawn.py enforces the one-respawn-per-task escalation cap only within a single run_worker() call (an if/else at spawn.py:1084), and never checks pipeline["tool_escalation_used"] before allowing escalation on a later, separate run_worker(task_id) invocation of the same task. Concretely: if the escalated (second) attempt itself returns status "held" (spawn.py:1144-1145, e.g. it again posts a needs_tool hold), the task is marked held and could be resumed later; on that later run_worker call, _hidden_tool_request(task_id) (spawn.py:1083) only reads the current bus result reason, with no check of prior pipeline["tool_escalation_used"], so a second escalation with a fresh budget reservation is possible, contradicting the spec (respawn capped at one per task). Read orchestrator/spawn.py around lines 1011-1158, focused on run_worker, _hidden_tool_request, and the held-status branch. Try to refute or confirm with concrete evidence.

inputs.claim: one-respawn-per-task cap is not enforced across separate run_worker invocations on the same task_id

acceptance: verdict confirmed, refuted, or uncertain with file:line evidence

result.note: pipeline['tool_escalation_used'] is stamped at spawn.py:1098 but never read/checked anywhere in spawn.py as a guard. The escalation branch (1084-1101) is gated only by disclosure_mode=='active' and _hidden_tool_request(task_id) finding a needs_tool: reason on the task's current bus result (311-314). Within one run_worker() call the escalation runs at most once structurally (single if/else, no loop), but nothing prevents a second, independent run_worker(task_id) invocation (e.g. after the task is held/requeued and redispatched by the daemon) from hitting the same branch and escalating again — tests (test_spawn.py:1254-1315) only verify single-call behavior, none exercise or assert a cross-invocation cap.
